title: CBR geodetic-datum migration, cadastral nonconversion, affected-holder remedy, and Maori-authority gate
hypothesis: A refusal-first authority matrix can prevent software from converting geodetic-coordinate guidance into a cadastral-boundary or rights decision without competent survey and legal authority, affected-holder participation, privacy governance, and Maori authority where relevant.
rollback: Return the matter to unknown and exact-gated, retain the refusal, expose no real location data, and route it to competent survey, legal, privacy, affected-holder, and Maori authorities.
boundary: Software and synthetic fixtures can establish only bounded structural behavior. They do not establish empirical GMUT confirmation, THOS effectiveness, production identity assurance, legal or cultural authority, independent reproduction, AGI/ASI, complete accessibility, exhaustive security, or Stage 20 readiness.
